utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, earlier today I sent an e-mail to the Defence and your legal officers regarding the discovery this morning of materials disclosed in the Popovic case last week that may contain Rule 68 material with respect to Mr. Masovic, the witness the Prosecution intended on calling this afternoon. It consists of a number of documents and is material that was not reviewed by my staff because when we initiated a computer search on his name, a search of our evidence collection of over 7 million documents, these documents were not flagged as relevant to him. This is in part because the body of material disclosed in the Popovic case relates to the International Commission of Missing Persons or ICMP, and primarily concerns their work on exhumations of Srebrenica in 1995. However, there is a relationship between Mr. Masovic's work and the work of the ICMP, and I believe my obligations under Rule 68 required that I review the material and that I notify the Chamber immediately. I had written earlier that I believed fairness required me to request the postponement of this witness's testimony until these documents could be reviewed and whatever documents containing Rule 68 could be disclosed. I assigned several lawyers the task of immediately reviewing these documents. They have done so and have identified eight documents, most of these are letters, a total volume of material is 31 pages. These documents primarily concern letters and e-mails written by former employee of Mr. Masovic, expressing dissatisfaction with Mr. Masovic's work. None of it directly related to Visegrad. It is my belief that they can be easily reviewed in approximately 30 to 60 minutes by the Defence. Mr. Van Hooydonk has already provided a copy of these documents to the Defence in court, and I have a copy for the Chamber should the Chamber wish to review these documents. I still think that fairness requires the Defence the benefit of having the opportunity to review these documents, and that's why, therefore, I on my own motion am asking the Chamber to postpone the calling of Mr. Masovic until tomorrow. As the Chamber will recall, the Chamber allotted Prosecution very limited time with Mr. Masovic and it was primarily for the introduction of his report and his prior testimony. It seems to me that it would be unfair to ask the Defence at this juncture to express a view as to the admissibility of those exhibits until they have had a chance to review this material. Also on the schedule for tomorrow is Mr. Ib Jul Hansen. While I still have some preparation to do in advance of his evidence, I do know that I will use less than half the time I originally estimated, and I estimate that I will use approximately 40 minutes. So I believe that we will be able to complete both Mr. Masovic's and Mr. Hansen's testimony in tomorrow's session and not lose any time in the Court's schedule. I apologise to the Defence and to the Chamber for this mishap, but I do see it as my duty to bring the attention to the Chamber and the Defence this late of discovery of Rule 68 material. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Of course it's very right and proper that you should bring this matter to the Chamber's attention. I just wanted to have clarified are you then asking for the postponement of Mr. Masovic's evidence until -- is it until next week or?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean I'll wait to hear what the Defence have to say, but I believe the volume of material now -- earlier this morning I was unable to ascertain the volume of material. I now can. It is 8 documents, 35 pages. I believe that is something that could be easily reviewed in 30 minutes to 60 minutes. It all relates to a single allegation by a single former employee. So I'm asking for an adjournment until tomorrow for Mr. Masovic's testimony and that tomorrow we would take both Mr. Masovic and Mr. Hansen, and I believe we could complete both of them tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see, yes. And you say it could be -- the document, in your view, could be reviewed within an hour, within 60 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the document, single-sided, and this is both the translation and the English. So it's really half of the amount that I'm holding up in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Yes. Yes, Mr. Ivetic. MR.IVETIC: Thank you, Your Honour. If I could just be heard briefly on this matter. With respect to the other materials that the Office of the Prosecution is in the view are not 68 materials, I would inquire of the total number of pages of the same and the number of attorneys or staff that the Prosecution had to review these to come to the analysis and conclusion that this is Rule 68 material for purposes of determining, of course, what other course of actions the Defence might take. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I do not know the exact number of the other documents. They are quite voluminous. I assigned two attorneys to the task and they did word searches for the name of Mr. Masovic on all the documents, and they identified the documents that had his name and read those. They are continuing to read the other documents, but they are clearly documents that relate to exhumations from Srebrenica, the Srebrenica massacre in 1995. I'm quite confident they have no bearing -- they have no mention of Mr. Masovic, have no bearing on this case directly and only concern the work of the ICMP for Srebrenica 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And so your examination-in-chief would take -- your examination of Mr. Masovic would take how long?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think approximately 10 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just 10 minutes. The Defence should then be in a position to proceed with the cross-examination. Mr. Masovic is the last witness or?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, there are two witnesses left this week, Your Honour, Mr. Masovic and Mr. Hansen, an investigator who will talk very briefly about identification procedures and -- that were used in the Vasiljevic case. I expect his evidence will be between 30 and 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Who is first?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Masovic was scheduled to be first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It might assist the Defence if he came last.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That is also possible that we could reverse them tomorrow if that would further assist the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, it seems to me that you should be in a position to commence cross-examination. MR.IVETIC: Tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. MR.IVETIC: I believe so. I don't know if that's, yeah, that's -- we are not objecting to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thanks. Well, we'll proceed in that manner then. If you call the other witness before Mr. Masovic, if that's practicable.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. I will do that. So all that remains then today would be the cross-examination of the witness from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. There's one other matter I wanted to raise, Mr. Groome. In response to an inquiry from the Bench yesterday, or was it the day before, following repeated complaints about the volume of ongoing disclosure, the Prosecution produced a list of the material disclosed to the Defence on Thursday, the 23rd of October. The document is entitled "Disclosure batch 47." It identifies 53 separate items or documents, half of which are said to relate to five witnesses still to testify. VG-094, two documents, Rule 66(a)(ii). Mr. Will Fadzel [phoen], ten documents, Rule 66(a)(ii). VG-042, five documents, two under Rule 66(a)(ii) and three under Rule 68. VG-131, ten documents, Rule 66(a)(ii). And VG-138, one document, Rule 68. The Chamber will require you before the end of the day to say precisely when these documents were disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been preparing a filing in light of what happened on that day. I didn't get to complete it this morning but I will have a complete filing explaining all of the documents, the disclosure dates and all the information you are requiring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness be called. Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, excuse me, Your Honour. A brief housekeeping matter in relation to exhibits from yesterday. So that yesterday's exhibits, the exhibits the extracts from the protocol book are dealt with uniformly, I note the Milan Lukic Defence also wanted unredacted versions of the extracts, I propose the following: Exhibit P162 is in redacted form at present, under seal. I therefore ask that Exhibit P162 be unsealed and be made public, and I ask that the unredacted version of those two pages be given a new exhibit number and be under seal. That brings all three extracts into line. And the ERN numbers we are talking about, 05452003 and 2004, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any comments, Mr. Alarid? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic? Yes, we'll do that. Let the witness be called, and it's cross-examination by Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid. Mr. Alarid, the Prosecutor spent one hour and 37 minutes in examining the witness, and that is the time that I will allow to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: As a maximum. Of course you don't have to use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I think we'd have an early day if that were the case. I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Madam, my name is Jason Alarid, and I am the attorney for Milan Lukic. I'd like to ask you a few questions about your testimony as well as your earlier statements. Can we do that today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, before we begin I'd like to advise you, have you ever been advised of the penalties for perjury in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You signed the statement back in August of 2008, did you -- were you advised that that statement constituted a statement under oath as if you were testifying in court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the fact that that statement could be used against you and that there were penalties for perjury if the statements contained therein were false, were you made aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You are aware that those same consequences apply to testimony in open court today and yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, first I'd like to address, and I'm going to use the proofing note given to me by the Prosecution yesterday as a guideline to my cross-examination, and I'd like to refer to paragraph 1 where -- which states specifically: "Prior to the proofing on 27 October 2008 ..." that was two days ago, correct, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When did you arrive in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 26th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long did you meet with the Prosecution over the course of two days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 27th from 9.00 to half past 12:00 or 1.00, I'm not entirely certain. And yesterday maybe for about an hour and a half, but I'm not positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And during the meeting between 9.00 until half past 12:00 or 1.00, whichever happens, who was present in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, his assistant, and an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what documents, in total, were you asked to review during those proofing sessions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two documents. No, as a matter of fact, two documents and the excerpts from the health centre protocol.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were those two documents an Official Note from August 18th, 1992, and a witness statement you gave 18th and 20th of August, 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in the proofing note that I'm holding before me says specifically that: "The witness had not seen the unsigned document RR154705, dated 18/8/92, concerning an interview with her. She was shown a similar document headed 'Gorazde' by officials in Bosnia-Herzegovina about two months ago. The statements are not her statements but she is familiar with some of the contents." Is that a fair and accurate relation to the 1992 report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, first I'd like to ask you, tell us about the time you were shown this Gorazde report that's similar to this by Bosnian officials, when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the first time I saw that report?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. It says a couple of months ago from the officials in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Where did that happen? How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early September this year agents of SIPA came to see me, and they showed me the note. That's what they said it was, but I'd never seen it before. And this was the very first I'd heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Explain to me what SIPA is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the police. State police. It's the police of the BH State Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, why did they come to tell you -- see you? Why did they come to show you this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were seeking information in relation to an entirely different investigation that was underway. I'm not sure that has any relevance for you in terms of me giving you more on that, but the BH state Prosecutor's Office is investigating a different person altogether. They just wanted to see whether I knew anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, if you say that the document you were shown there entitled "Gorazde" was similar to the one you were shown by the Prosecution in your proofing session, was it identical or similar, simply with a different heading?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't just a heading. I'll tell you about the first document that I saw in September. It said that I'd provided that statement in Gorazde. It's just that I've never been to Gorazde at all in my entire life; that's the first thing. Secondly, that document reads: "Official Note." In September when I was shown that document, it didn't say "Official Note." Another thing that I observed after I'd gone through the document, that's how you refer to it anyway, so in September I looked at the document and there were four or five references to the 14th of June -- now that I've read it again, I think I only spotted a single reference, if. All I can tell you about that document, I am no lawyer myself, but that is not a statement. It doesn't qualify as a statement, as far as I know. Secondly, I didn't provide that, nor indeed did I provide any statements. I know how the document came about and if necessary, I'd be happy to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That would be my next question, ma'am. How were these documents generated even if you -- and explain that you've never been to Gorazde, where were you when you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not the person interviewed, that's the first thing. Secondly, I was in Zenica. The interviewees on that occasion were five or six persons, interviewed all together. No notes were taken. There were two interviewers who interviewed five or six persons who were all in the same room. At a later stage, unbeknownst to us and without informing us, they drew up that document. When we arrived in Zenica in August 1992, there were several people there from several different institutions. We didn't really know who they were because sometimes they introduced themselves and sometimes they didn't. They wanted to know how we got there, how we had fled, where we had found accommodation, that sort of thing. It was that sort of subject matter that was discussed, and this interview took place with several persons all at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So this was a general report, but you understand that the 18th August 1992 appears that it's an interview by yourself? Can you concede that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not even sure if that was on the 18th of August, and it is not that I was interviewed myself. There was no report and I was not interviewed myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you are saying that you gave no information to police authorities in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said. I don't think you understood me well. I said there were several of us there and we spoke, but it wasn't before later on that anything was recorded, but they didn't attribute any of the quotes in that document. They drew the whole thing up together, and they just recorded whatever they remembered because they weren't taking any notes during the actual interview when they were interviewing us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And let me ask you this, though, it says you agree with some of the contents of that report though; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I just want to be clear, the proofing note says she's familiar with some of the contents. I know she's answered the question, but could I ask my friend be clear when he is putting these suggestions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm only going to ask a couple of questions regarding the 1992 note, and then I'm going to move on to 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In the Official Note it states that: "Until the departure of the JNA Yugoslav Army from Visegrad in 19 May 1992, the situation in the area was tolerable, meaning that there were constant identity card checks, inspections, confiscation of vehicles and the like." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure the sentence makes sense to me. I don't think I'm even able to understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, during -- before the JNA left, there were constant identity card checks; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were there constant inspections of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were confiscations of vehicles occurring during the time the JNA was in town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Not at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all the time. Not constantly. Some vehicles were seized but it wasn't by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is it true that as the JNA members were leaving, they torched houses of prominent Muslims in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So before the Uzice Corps left, there were no homes burning in Visegrad is what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They withdrew from Visegrad. They did not torch houses when they left, but fires did occur while the JNA was in Visegrad as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. So you wouldn't know if it was the JNA starting those fires or not because you weren't there; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean I wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, were you a personal witness to every house burning in Visegrad area before the JNA left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you don't know who started those fires and it could have been the Uzice Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So it could have been the Uzice Corps that were burning houses; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is possible in the villages. Anybody who wanted to could do torching. Nobody of us knew about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, is it true that as the JNA was leaving the members of the White Eagles remained in Visegrad, who had arrived with the JNA, and were stationed at the Vilina Vlas and later at the Visegrad Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it true that the leader of this paramilitary unit was a man known as Cale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard of the man, but I never saw him. I heard about him from others but I never saw him personally myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Be as description and exhaustive as possible, tell me what you heard about Cale from others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't hear anything special about him. I heard that somebody by that name was there, that he had arrived, that he was a commander of some kind, that he had been accommodated in the Visegrad Hotel. And that's all. Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In the Official Note it says that he had a son called Nenad who was -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have absolutely no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But it was your understanding that Cale was originally from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And had you heard that he was from Obrenovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, there's also a reference to a Branimir Savovic in the statement on page 2. Is it true that he was an economist who worked in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He worked with my husband, so I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is it true that he was the president of the SDS in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it true that he was a leader in Visegrad at the time of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In the Official Note of 1998, relating to supposedly interviewing you, it states that Branimir Savovic was in direct contact with the White Eagles and he was the main organiser of everything that happened in Visegrad and the consequences that followed. Is that true or had you heard that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, but I didn't understand you. Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In the Official Note of 1992, ma'am. I'm going off that. I understand you've looked at it. I'm not talking about your statement of 2008. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Excuse me, Judge. That's my faux pas. 1992 is the Official Note. 2008 is her official statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But let me just ask you this: Had you heard that? Was there an understanding of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you, I never said that. I didn't say whether I'd heard about it or anything else. I never said anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, in clarification I'm not asking that anymore. What I'm asking you is just other than this statement, had you heard that from anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you -- had you heard that his associate was Dusko Andric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether Dusko Andric was an associate of his, but I did know Dusko Andric, I knew him personally. Now whether he was an associate of Branimir Savovic, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you know Mr. Andric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everybody knew everybody else in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know Risto Perisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that he was the commander of the police in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a professor at the secondary school. Now, when the war began, he was the commander or chief in the police, I don't know what title he had, what it was called at the time, but yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, and to make a difference between the titles, isn't it true that the chief of police was Drago Tomic? Dragan, excuse me. Commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Tomic and him. I don't know what their titles were but they held positions, both of them, in the then -- what was it called, the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you know who Drago Gavrilovic was, Dragomir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to forward you to the -- well, actually let me just ask you a few more background questions. You said that you were interviewed in the sense of several people being present in 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so people --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I understand, Mr. Cole, I apologise. We can redact.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I just ask that that passage about where she's currently living be redacted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, since you've been living in the same place for all this time, would it be fair to say that investigators knew where to find you if they needed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason, I guess, I ask you that is because has anyone ever questioned you again on what you witnessed in Visegrad since 1992 and between 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you keep a journal or any diaries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you keep a -- so you didn't keep a journal or anything to help you remember things from 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you still with your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you still talk to your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is your mother still around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is your sister still around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you know if any of them have been interviewed by either Bosnian or ICTY authorities in regards to what they may have witnessed in relation to what you've witnessed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because it's my understanding based on your testimony yesterday that your husband had some powerful testimony regarding the Varda situation; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't understand that properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Explain it to me then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband just talked to me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, but my point being is, you've told now investigators that he was around and involved in your situation because you were all fleeing together, and so I'm wondering why no one has spoken to your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again you misunderstood me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So explain it to me again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. My husband left Visegrad a month before me. We weren't together. It was only after five months that my husband came to where I was. My husband went towards Gorazde and he was in the village of Nezuci, opposite the Dusce settlement on the other side of the Drina River, the opposite bank. It's about one to one and a half kilometres away from town, whereas I was in town myself and we contacted over the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So, ma'am, if your husband left a month before you and you left June 17th, that means he left May 17th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. No, it doesn't, because I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, but you do know a month; correct? Four weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know roughly because the Uzice Corps had still not left town when he left, because the Uzice Corps was still there, and I know that there were some checkpoints at the beginning -- one in both ends of the bridge, and a Serb friend of ours saved my husband and drove him to the village of Nezuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who is the -- can you tell me the name of the Serb that helped your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, but I'd like to state it in private session because I don't want to -- anybody who helped me in that situation to have any problems after my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, between 1992 and 2008, I think the question I want to ask you is: Did you talk to anybody about what happened in Visegrad that last two or three weeks you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you converse with your family, in passing over the years, about what happened that June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How often would you talk about it amongst the family over the years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, really, I can't really say how many times, but we did discuss it. In recent years, perhaps rarely, but we did discuss it. When the graves were dug up, perhaps a little more, because my sister and her children because of the DNA analysis were called very frequently to give blood samples because they are still searching for her husband. He still hasn't been found. So perhaps we discussed it a little more frequently because of those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: This is the same sister that went with you to find your mother; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... investigators, and it's also the same sister that was with you when the people were abducted from your mother-in-law's apartment building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, my sister wasn't with me on that occasion. She went back to her own house, to her own flat and her children.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where did your mother go when you got back from finding her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother stayed where we had found her. She lived with the neighbours. They accommodated her there. They would take some food and then they stayed there for four days, and then they were all taken into a bus and brought to the square in Visegrad and then in the convoy to Olovo four days after we had found her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So at the very least your sister would be able to confirm about finding your mom; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean, finding our mom? We went to look for her. She didn't answer the phone, and we weren't able to contact her, and news reached us from the stories being told around town that women in her neighbourhood had been killed. And that's why we went to see what was happening and where our mother was, and we found an empty house when we got there. The house was open, unlocked, but empty. And there's a bridge near my mother's house and there were some Serb neighbours living there who told us that our mother was alive, that they had seen her, and that she was somewhere in the woods in the surrounding parts with a couple of other neighbours. And that's how the two of us went to look for her and found her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, first things first. I'd like to go through that day because that's an important day. You say this is June 10th; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you understand that in your statement of just two months ago, being August 18th and 20th of 2008, you didn't give a specific date for that; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Not only did you give a specific date but you gave a date that you thought it was around June 7th because you looked at the protocol book, according to your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That is right, and I didn't say it was on the 7th of June. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's why I said that it might have been that day because her husband and son had been killed so that might have happened that day, although I didn't claim that that was actually the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, let's go through the day you found your mother step by step, okay? What time did you get up in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether we even went to sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. If you didn't go to sleep, regardless of that, when did you find out your mom was missing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew that she had been missing for two days, or rather, we hadn't had any contact with her for two days. From Sunday -- Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, we didn't have any contact with her. She didn't answer the phone, she didn't ring us. So on the Tuesday we decided -- well, everybody advised us not to go because it's some 7 or 8 kilometres away from town. However, we decided that if we still failed to contact our mother and we had heard -- I think it was a Tuesday, the Tuesday when we heard that an incident had taken place up there, that is to say, when the women were killed and burned in a house, that that was when we decided to go and see what was happening. So we set out on Wednesday morning --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just a moment. Just a moment. Where were you when you were discussing and deciding to go see what was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who are you referring to? Who was where?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who else did you say? My sister, you mean. Did you mean where we were, my sister and I?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my sister was visiting me with her children in my flat, not my flat actually, but I was with my children at my mother-in-law's because we would move around every three or four days. We wouldn't spend time in the same flat because they would come and search our houses and flats. So we moved around, and I happened to be in my mother-in-law's flat at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just a moment. Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we go to page 5 of the English, please. And the corresponding page -- and paragraph 17 being the reference, so the corresponding paragraph in Bosnian is on page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you see paragraph 17, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this statement was typed to you -- for you after two days or a lengthy interview by the Office of the Prosecutor; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you of course had discussed this situation over the years with your family; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you mean the specific situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. So otherwise, this situation had just sat in your mind, in your memories for 15 years before you got to tell it to the Prosecutor; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd ask you to read paragraph 17 for the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the whole thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In June 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I question that procedure. Why do you want her to read the whole thing? Would you like to direct her to a particular sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I could, Your Honour. It's -- I guess very relevant to read the entire thing, but I'll just ask the questions more pointedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Isn't it true that in paragraph 17 of your original statement, August 2008, you stated that at the time Milan Lukic came to your door, he rang the doorbell; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And according to paragraph 17 of your statement, you could not recall the exact time but: "... I believe it was mid-morning because we had already been out of bed for some time and had eaten our breakfast..." isn't that what you wrote or signed to in August 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I did note that I couldn't remember the exact time. I couldn't remember the exact date either. Nevertheless, I was prompted by my husband and my mother-in-law when I spoke to them. You must understand, it's been 16 years and you need something to jog your memory. You don't remember certain things right off the bat. Your memory needs jogging in order for you to be able to remember certain dates. Another thing that I can tell you, it wasn't just Milan Lukic who came to my home. There were three or four other times that groups of people came. I had no idea who they were, what they were after or who they were after. They walk into your house, they turned the whole place upside-down, they scare your children and you, which is quite a chaotic experience. So sometimes if you mix up a couple of dates or a couple of times of day, I don't think anyone should be surprised. I think you get the point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would you agree that there's a significant difference between mid-morning and after 5.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I just told you that it wasn't on that day that I could remember the exact date and the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, according to paragraph 17 of your August 2008 statement, it appears that you -- at the time the doorbell rang, you and your family were just hanging around in the flat before the doorbell rang. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can all see the statement and as I read it, there's nothing about hanging around in the flat. So I wonder if the question could be specific or a passage put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Pardon my use of slang for "hanging around," but I think the witness understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, just rely on the statement. You can't do better than to cite the statement itself, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that according to paragraph 17, you referenced, even though not knowing the exact time, your belief that it was mid-morning because you had just finished your -- eaten your breakfast, and you had been out of bed for sometime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true, not about that day anyway. As I just told you, I mixed up the two events. If necessary, I can explain this development too, one of the two that I got mixed up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you saying there's been a mix-up? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A day before Milan Lukic's arrival, two men came, showed up at our door in grey uniforms and with Montenegrin accents. They were there that morning. They harassed me and my children. They locked me up in a room. There was this young man who wasn't even 20, I think he tried to rape me. My children were there. My daughter was 9 and a half and my son was 6. They dashed into the room. He then called his mate, who had some sort of a black vest on him, and they both came. This was that morning, and I got the dates mixed up. However, when I brought this up with my husband and my mother-in-law and told them that I couldn't quite remember exactly the date in which Milan Lukic arrived, they reminded me that it was the same day that I went out looking for my mother. When Milan Lukic came and parked outside my mother-in-law's building, at that moment I was talking to my husband on the phone, but there is no link between that and what happened in Varda in my mind. I'm simply remembering that it was the same day that my husband told me that we should run away, that we should leave our flat because there were all those things happening in Dusce and in Varda. He didn't say that it was Milan Lukic that was doing all these things in Varda or in Dusce, because he wasn't there to see it for himself. He was elsewhere. The only reason I'm mentioned this is to cite it as a reason -- as the reason I remembered the date when this occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, but one thing that's very important is time of day, and you either remember a death being in the morning or in the afternoon, and it appears to me, that according to paragraph 17, the entire incident occurred in the morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I just explained, isn't it? I couldn't remember the time of day. And these developments came in a quick succession and these things would happen, three, four, five times a day, but here is one thing that I could remember because it was that afternoon and I had returned from my mother's village on the 5.00 p.m. bus. I spoke to my husband on the phone as soon as I arrived in the flat. Meaning, I couldn't have reached my flat after that bus in half an hour. It could have been at half past 5.00 or 6.00, at the very earliest, because the bus left my mother's village at 5.00 p.m. and it would have taken me at least 15 minutes from the bus terminal to reach my mother-in-law's place, 10 to 15 minutes. So it could only have been around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court assistant please refer to paragraph 20 of what is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, isn't it true that the telephones didn't work during that time period in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that there was no telephone communication between -- or it was intermittent due to the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they kept operating throughout. The last time I spoke to my husband on the phone was on the 15th of June which was when I decided to leave Visegrad. That very day I spoke to my husband on the phone, therefore the phone lines were very much operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like you to refer to 20, paragraph 20 of your statement, please. And this is your reference point of which you recalled on August 18th and 20th, 2008, on why you believe the murders, including Alija Selak, occurred around June 7th, not June 10th. And isn't it true that you stated and signed and affirmed that: "I cannot be sure of the exact date of these murders but it was certainly around the 7th of June, and this entry in the protocol book leaves me to believe that this was the date."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On or about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But yet, ma'am, again, specifically you recall being at home in the morning according to your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which morning do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, the unknown date in June that you referred to in paragraph 17 of your statement, you believe it's mid-morning. I understand you don't know the exact time, but you believed it was mid-morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What time did it get dark in Visegrad early June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 8.00, 9.00 p.m. thereabouts. It was summer, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so would it be fair to say that after you got off the bus from Uzice, the sun would have been in an entirely different part of the sky than it is in mid-morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be quite honest, this wasn't exactly the sort of thing that we were keeping track of at the time, the position of the sun. For the most part, you know, the thing that we were viewing were the cellar walls in which we were hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I thought you were in a fourth floor flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What cellar are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the cellars in which we were sleeping. We hardly ever slept in our flats. We were too scared to sleep in our flats. We would get some clothes, get our kids and then try to locate a basement or a cellar in one of the nearby buildings to spend the night in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But it's my understanding that you were being harassed in your apartment during the day, and you just accounted for the day before you were almost raped by a soldier in grey. Why would you be in an apartment the very next day to be assaulted in the same way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why weren't you in the cellar because of that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had to go back to feed our children, get them a change of clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, according to paragraph 2 of the proofing statement, it states: "The witness has seen some of the Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic trial proceedings on the internet and on television including pictures of Milan Lukic." Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm assuming you have a computer to watch this on the internet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you follow the Mitar Vasiljevic trial before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When did you start following this trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't follow this trial on a regular basis either. I use the SENSE Agency covering the work of the Tribunal. Each Saturday morning one of the Bosnian channels shows reports, coverage of this trial. I couldn't follow the whole thing closely on the internet because I'm busy doing other things, I have my work, but I have read a couple of reports from the trial. There are normally images included in these reports and you tend to see the same sort of thing on TV as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true during those Sense reports, they flash current pictures identifying my client Milan Lukic every time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it's every single time, but yes, that has been the case generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And they identify him by his name as they flash to him here in court? They flash to me as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't remember whether they identify him when they show the image. But what is known is that it's the Lukic case, when they give a report on that. Now, I didn't especially look to see whether they put a name to the face, but we know that it's the trial, they announce the trial as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, it appears to me that you are exhausting the questioning that you have of this witness. We're going to take the break now, and you'll have another 10 minutes at a maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you don't need 10 minutes, then so be it. Let us adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I ought to have said from the outset that in the absence of Judge Van den Wyngaert, Judge David and I sit pursuant to the provisions of Rule 15 bis. Now the court deputy would like a few minutes to clarify something.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Regarding the unredacted version of Exhibit P162, under seal, which bears ERN number 05452003-1 will become Exhibit P167. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, I would like to point your attention to a couple of points since my time is running short. Isn't it true, ma'am, that yesterday on direct examination, and I'm referring to page 77 of the transcript, that you said that you never saw anyone but Milan Lukic drive that Passat? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like the court assistant, please, to go back to the same document we had on the screen, paragraph 25, P161.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you qualified your statement of August 2008 again saying that you didn't know if it was Milan's brother in the car that day; correct? You didn't know Milan's brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But I'd like you to look at the bottom of page 25, please, which would be on the next page of the B/C/S version. The last sentence. I'd just like you to read the last sentence. Now, at this point in time you also said that, of course, you didn't see Sredoje in the car, but you did see Milan's brother following behind in the Passat. Doesn't that mean somebody else was driving the Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That is what I wanted to have corrected. I asked to have that corrected. There was a mistake either in understanding or in the translation. Anyway, the Passat was standing at the end of the bridge and the boy who got out of the Passat and leaned against the door to the Passat and stood by the Passat while Milan Lukic was going behind the man that they later took into the Passat. The Passat remained there, remained standing there, and Milan shot up in the air from an automatic rifle. And I don't know how it came to be said here that it was Sredoje, because Sredoje wasn't there at all. The boy was there and passers by said that it was Milan's brother but I didn't know Milan's brother myself, nor did I know that he had a brother or whether that was his brother at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, just a few side questions. Are you -- do you associate with or have you ever known a Dragolje Tasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now. The name sounds familiar, and there might have been several people with that same name. I certainly didn't socialize with the person, associate with him. But as I say, the name does ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I apologise for mispronouncing it, it's Dragolja. Female.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragojla.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not familiar. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know Ankica Savovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know Ankica Savovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you know her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as we knew everyone. We knew people by sight. We didn't socialize but we all knew each other, and I think that she was Brano Savovic's wife, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you ever go to a cafe or did you frequent a cafe owned by Tasic's brother in the company of Smajic Brane, otherwise known as Zika. And it's Smiljic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, according to your proofing note, you bring up June 14th, and you also, in your original statement of August, you bring up June 14th, but you only bring it up in August in paragraph 28. Can we have 28 on the screen, please. And can you see there in the sentence -- second to the last sentence in paragraph 28: "My mother left in a convoy on 14 June and somewhere near Olovo the Serbs stopped the convoy, took off 64 men and killed them. One of the bus drivers from the convoy of 14 June called me and told me that they had stopped the buses and taken the men." Isn't that what you stated in August 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the paragraph we just looked at before that -- or excuse me, in paragraph 27, you do state that you saw Milan Lukic on the bus that you left on; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him in this bus, too, when my mother left, and I also saw him in the bus that I was in on the 17th of June when I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, isn't it true in your statement of August 2008, you don't even mention being on the bus with your mother in June 14th, much less seeing Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly I don't mention it, yes. Perhaps the investigator didn't ask me, or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Don't you think it's important? I mean, you are giving a statement to investigator regarding Milan Lukic, don't you think it's important to mention everything about Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Including whether her mother was on the bus with her?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No. Whether she was on the bus with her mother and saw Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But she just explained, she said she might not have been asked whether her mother was there with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, have you read the indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you aware of the charges in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not read the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you aware of the charges in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly. For crimes that he committed during that time, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you know that one of the counts in the indictment coincidentally involves June 10th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know coincidentally that one of the counts in the indictment involves June 14th?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, it's a very loaded question, coincidentally. I'm not sure that I understand what it means. I wonder if my friend could be a little bit more --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, as a proffer, Your Honour, I can make this, is in the original statement of August 2008 and if offered as an alibi witness or an alibi rebuttal witness, this witness originally gave a statement that really just by virtue of authenticating the protocol book of June 7th entry, that I can see how is evidence rebutting the alibi related to our alibi proffer as to that date in particular. Coincidentally, between August of 2008 and her proofing notes of yesterday morning that amount to another statement, she now specifically sees Milan Lukic on two relevant new dates in the indictment that were never mentioned before. June 10th, regarding the day she went to get her mom and then now sees Milan Lukic on the bridge even though she didn't know that before. And June 14th, the day of Pionirska Street and happens to see him in the square the day of the fire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Just a minute. If you want to put to her something in relation to that, put it to her. Don't shy away from it. You put what you want to her, that is your duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the basis of the instructions that you have and you can't be criticized.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, isn't it true that in your new statement of yesterday or your proofing notes of yesterday, you mentioned that you heard personally that he was looking for a Kurspahic member of the family; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you also state that he tried to take off a man called Kustura; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that. That was something that I was told by my sister's sister-in-law, and she said that that was a school friend of his. And that this school friend of his called him to come out of the bus and that a neighbour from Bosanska Jagodina prevented him from doing that and told him to leave that Kustura person in the bus. And I was told that he was left in the bus and that he didn't touch him anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And ma'am, isn't it true that you have knowledge that the Kurspahic family name was the family name of the victims of the Pionirska Street fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, coincidentally though, ma'am, is that you claim to see a large group of civilians from Zupa in the square June 14th; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you now state as of yesterday that a large number of soldiers herded those people to the Mahala neighbourhood; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the Mahala neighbourhood is where Pionirska Street is; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We call that entire settlement Mahala. And as soon as you go over the Rzavski bridge to the exit of Visegrad, the local population called that whole area Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You know that after the Pionirska Street fire the news about it got out; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about that on the 15th of June in the morning. I heard about that close to my home and that's why I decided to leave town.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Including the fact that the Kurspahic family was the main victims of that fire; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. For many years I worked in the health centre and in the outpatients department in Zupa but I didn't know the population, local population very well. I didn't visit it much. Perhaps I had been on visits to the area maybe just ten times, so it wasn't an area of the municipality that I was well acquainted with.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That is not the question I wanted to ask you, ma'am. The question I wanted to ask you is: Isn't it true you knew the name Kurspahic as being the victims in the fire as you heard the rumours spread about the fire the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. At that point in time, we didn't know who the people were. We didn't know that then. Let me explain one thing to you. On that morning, we heard that 50 people had been burnt, and then somebody else turned by and said that 200 people were burned. Then somebody came by and said that three houses with 100 people in them had been burned, and so this gave rise to general panic because we didn't have the real information, the proper information. Somebody heard that it had happened, then it was passed on by word of mouth and the information was distorted. So in the end you didn't know what was correct and what wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Then going back to a question you answered affirmatively a little while ago which is that you knew -- you now know the Kurspahic's were the victims of that fire. When did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I found that out -- maybe that happened while I was in Visoko, in actual fact, when the next group arrived and when the new people arrived, the people who left Visegrad the latest. So it might have been a month later in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I'll give you another two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So wouldn't it be illogical that Milan Lukic would be looking for a Kurspahic before the fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what would be logical and what not. All I do know is that Milan Lukic looked for a young girl named Kurspahic in that bus, and I don't remember her first name. All I know is that he was looking for the girl. And I know that he took somebody's ID because a woman said that she was there, so he asked a woman to show her ID papers, she showed him her ID and he threw it back to her. Now, what is logical and what isn't, I really wouldn't like to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And ma'am, do you think it's an incredible coincidence that you left August 2008 being an alibi rebuttal for one date June 7th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, don't put that question to the witness. I'm not allowing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What jogged your memory specifically to include that you were seeing Milan Lukic on both June 10th and June 14th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's the question you should have put long ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, don't you think you should have remembered that before August 2008 since it was such a powerful memory, combined with the powerful memory of being reunited with your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I did not remember that. No, I've never forgotten that. It's not that I remembered it, I've never forgotten it, so there was no need for me to remember something that I've never forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, apparently you forgot it August 2008.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I never forgot that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you mean, that wasn't in her statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It was not in her -- excuse me, Your Honour. It was not in her statement of August 2008, the coordination between the rescue of her mother, or the discovery of her mother, rather, and this incident on the bridge, combined with the fact that she placed the incident on the bridge on the mid-morning in her first statement and after she got back after 5.00 p.m. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that's what you should have asked her --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I was trying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- in my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was trying to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation as to why that wasn't in your statement of August 2008.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. When I gave my statement to the investigator of the Tribunal, at that point in time we were speaking about convoys and saving the people from Visegrad. And from that time on we discussed the convoy. It was the first convoy -- or, rather, the first convoy was around the 25th and 26th of May that left Visegrad, and then the convoy of the 14th of June and the convoy of the 14th of June, so that we did not discuss the details. And when I gave my statement, the investigator didn't ask me about those things because we'd already done that in the sort of abridged statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: A couple more questions based on her response to your question, Your Honour. And really just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just one question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, can you explain to the Court how you were approached to testify in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean who approached me? Who contacted me?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who, the timing, all of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was called up on the telephone by the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure exactly when, but it was some 20 days or one month before I gave my actual statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was it discussed in that initial phone conversation what you would be valuable to this Court for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not much. I was only told -- I was only asked whether I would accept giving a statement for The Hague Tribunal, and I was told that it was for the Milan Lukic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: My point being is, was there any direction given to you as to what you would be talking about, what direction you would be going towards here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't discuss that. The instructions that I was given referred to my work in the health centre, that's what I was told at the time. That is to say, that it would refer to the treatment of Milan Lukic and my engagement in the health centre at Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You can't take this any further, Mr. Alarid. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, one more question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I'm not allowing any more. You cannot take it any further. You have elicited from the witness as much as you can get. I know what you are trying to get and you can't get anything further. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, madam.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My name is Djuro Cepic. I'd like to introduce myself, and I'm Defence counsel for Sredoje Lukic. I have to address you with your code name, not out of disrespect to you. Would you listen carefully to my questions. I'll try and be as precise as possible, and could I ask you to give short and precise answers as well so that we can get through what we have here as quickly as possible. Now, my colleague's already mentioned this but you talked to the representatives of the Tribunal on the 27th of October, and during that discussion there was my learned friend Stevan Cole present, Justin Brownstone, his assistant, and Dominique Vorkapic-Kolic as the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: On that occasion when you discussed the events of the 20th of May when a red Passat came to the health centre, you said that you think that Sredoje Lukic might have been in the back seat of the car.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was sitting on the back seat of the car. However, and I remember this, because Niko Vujicic and Milan Lukic were laughing cynically.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. That is not what I was asking you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to also say --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just wait a moment. Please listen to my questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was going to answer what you wanted to know about Sredoje.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to say that that's why I remembered Sredoje because Sredoje --

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, rather than having this between the counsel and the witness, if the witness has further material in her answer, she should be allowed to give it without being stopped by counsel and that it seems to me that she's trying to get to the essence of this question even if it's taking a little longer than counsel would like.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree. Let her complete the answer. You were saying that you wanted to say that that is why you remembered Sredoje because Sredoje did something. Please complete the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember him because, out of the three of them, it was only Sredoje behaved, if we can say decently then decently. He wasn't making any grimaces, he wasn't laughing cynically, he was just sitting quietly at the back. While the other two, Milan Lukic opened the car window, laughed cynically, and Niko Vujicic did the same, and then they switched the motor on and drove off. Whereas Sredoje Lukic didn't even look at us. And I remember gaining the impression that Sredoje, at that point in time, felt uncomfortable. And that's what I wanted to tell you. Because of the three of them at that point in time, at least that's the impression I gained, because I was upset, we were all crying when that happened and that's why I remember Sredoje. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, my time is limited so please try and give me short answers so that we can get through all the questions I have to ask you. Now, why did you tell my colleague that you think he was there, not that you claimed that he was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember I said I think. Maybe I did. While I was recounting the events possibly I used the word "I think," the term "I think," but it's an assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, I have no reason to doubt my colleagues either. I believe fervently that they wrote down the truth and wrote down your words. You said you "think." Now, do you still "think" or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it is possible that I used the verb "think." I might have said I think because when you answer questions you can use that sort of expression, but I'm quite certain that he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that, just in a moment. Madam, yesterday you were shown a piece of paper with the identifying names of two individuals. Could we show that list to the witness again. Do you have it in front of you? Yes, you do. Do you see VG-032 on that list?
