utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now that gentleman worked together with you in the health centre; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was a dental technician and worked in a completely different building in the dentistry department. He made prosthesis, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: He worked in the same hospital, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same health centre, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And you agree with me that 32 is an honourable and well respected citizen; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You also agree that his assertions and allegations are trustworthy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You would lend credence to his allegations, would you not, in relation to this specific situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he claims he is one hundred percent certain, why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, he testified under oath before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please wait until I finish my question. He testified under oath that he had seen Milan Lukic and another person he didn't know on that day, but when prompted about Sredoje Lukic, he said he had never heard anything bad about that person, and by that same token, he had not seen him that morning. What would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I not agree to this other person saying that he had not seen Sredoje Lukic? No reason for me not to agree; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You will also agree that he was better placed and had a clearer view of the situation than you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. He could not possibly have been better placed than me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You still want to say something, Mr. Cole?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: No, thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I thought not, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. We missed the part of transcript page 56, we missed the answer which would be in the line 24.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Line 24. You said in line 24: "You will also agree that he was better placed and with a better view than you." And her answer was: "That's not true. He could not possibly have been better placed than me."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, but maybe I didn't mark correctly. The question -- previous question than the line 24. Actually that question starts from line 17 and it is quite long question and actually her answer is from 21st row ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let me just read it. Line 17 before it goes off my screen. "He testified under oath he had seen Milan Lukic and another person he did not know on that day, but when prompted about Sredoje Lukic, he said he had never heard anything bad about that person." Did you continue the question or? Well, I tell you what just ask the question again, if you think that there was no answer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, let me repeat my question and you please repeat the answer for me. In relation to VG-32, and the situation outside the health centre. His evidence shows clearly that he did not see Sredoje Lukic on that day but rather Milan Lukic and another lad. When prompted about Sredoje Lukic, he said he had never heard anything bad about that person. You'll agree with his assertion; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I agree with him. He says he didn't hear anything bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't stand, Your Honour, before this question was asked, again, because it was already on the record, but in my submission it's inappropriate to put the testimony of other witnesses to a witness and ask them to comment on them. It's a dangerous area to get into. She doesn't know specifically, it may be paraphrased, so I would object to this type of questioning of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I agree with it. There are times when you can use another witness's evidence, but I think you tend to overdo it. It seems to become the main plank in your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You consistently use that technique. That is the -- that's your main line of questioning, Mr. Cepic. Another witness said so and so, do you agree. So I'd like you to move on to another area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, in nature to the Court's comments though, I mean, that is an essential component of this case which is witnesses seeing supposedly the same thing yet having greatly divergent explanations, and that is a problem. How do we address that? Final submissions is one way, but we do need to at times to address it with the witnesses because they see the same things --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But you can call those witnesses. And it's for the Chamber to make its own assessment as to who it believes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If I could add, Your Honour, it's a matter for submissions, not a matter for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I spent two years in a previous mass case and sometimes, not always, and it was not the base for my cross-examination, I confronted some allegations and statements to other witnesses related to some incidents. Thank you very much. And I will change the topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about this: I find it a little strange that between 1992 and August 2008 you never thought to go to the police, you never thought to get in touch with the ICTY investigators, you never spoke to anyone at all, in fact, although it was your civil duty under the law and criminal procedure in Bosnia-Herzegovina that has been applying throughout to report any crime that you might be aware of and anything you know about that. Why did you violate a provision of the criminal code of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I violated any provision of any code or law, criminal or otherwise. All of these matters had been reported all ready. Not just reported but also debated in the public media. Given the situation, I simply didn't believe that it was my duty to go and report anything at all that I believe was generally known. However, now we are looking at a different situation. I'm summoned by a Tribunal, this Tribunal or any other Tribunal to give evidence. I will always oblige. There's no doubt about that. But I simply didn't see fit for me to go and report something that had already been bandied about in the media and well known to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. So your evidence is you didn't feel a need to report a crime, although you knew that this crime was being investigated. You consider yourself an eyewitness; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do consider myself an eyewitness. I can't say I didn't see something if I did, can I? Should I be asked to state otherwise, I will refuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. It's been 16 years, isn't it just ever so slightly strange perhaps that in August 2008 suddenly you give evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even now I didn't volunteer myself to give evidence. It wasn't me who decided it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How did this reach you, this whole thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We just might get to that. Madam, are you familiar with the lie of the land in Visegrad and its surroundings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know the location of a village called Povjestaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might be roughly familiar with its location. I know it's across the Drina. You take the old bridge across the river, but I don't think I could pinpoint it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But it's outside town, it's not a part of Visegrad, is it? You will agree with that; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you are right on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 25 of your statement. [In English] In the e-court system there was a statement from 2008, P16 ... [Interpretation] Before the statement shows up just to gain time, Islam Cormehic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: He went missing -- the centre of town taken to the bridge and taken towards --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get where.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was this car that took the bridge in the direction of the Mahala and then they took a turning to Visegradska Banja. That is the road to Visegradska Banja.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So that's your testimony; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cormehic was born sometime in 1956 or 1957, roughly speaking; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not really certain. He was a shopkeeper in the Jugoplastika

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: together because this was a funeral. This was Behija Zukic's funeral and we met there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. In this paragraph you talk about his disappearance. We may, therefore, conclude that Islam Cormehic disappeared in the centre of town, at the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the old bridge, the Rzav bridge which is another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. I know, thank you. The one near the SUP building right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [In English] 2D04-0070.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, let's see what an ICRC document has to say about this. [In English] Could we have the fourth page, please. Under number 94, please. Zoom in 94? [Interpretation] Madam, the ICRC claims that Mr. Islam Cormehic went missing in Povjestaca. You have just confirmed that this was not in Visegrad, rather outside Visegrad. Your testimony seems to run counter to an ICRC document. Where does this discrepancy come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it says Povjestaca does it does it mean that he was born there or that he went missing there?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: He went missing there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I just know what I saw. I saw the people who were there. I talked to Islam Cormehic on the bridge. We were there together, and then he was put into that car.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. And now let's talk about the old bridge. You say you saw Milan Lukic and the persons who were with him. Did they stop midway across the old bridge near sofa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, near sofa. Midway across the bridge, but I can't say exactly at which point. Actually, I don't think I even understood. Did you ask me about the car or did you ask me about the persons?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The killings that you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the specific killings that I witnessed? It wasn't at Sofa. If you are asking about the specific killings.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that later. Madam, we are about to locate the exact paragraph, it's 22, paragraph 22 of your statement. [Previous translation continues] ... Now, as we are waiting for the paragraph to come up, let me just return briefly to the health centre and this situation when you saw Sredoje Lukic, allegedly. You talk about that in your statement, more specifically in paragraph 9 of your statement where you describe Niko Vujicic, Sredoje Lukic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us see paragraph 9 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You provide a description there. You see paragraph 9, madam, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You provide a description of Sredoje Lukic, Niko Vujicic. We'll be going back to that later on. And then in paragraph 12, can we have paragraph 12, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is it you are pointing out to her in paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just the description of Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The description. Now we are going to paragraph 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 12, Your Honour, witness describes situation with red Passat, Milan Lukic and others in the front. Just about she testified a couple minutes ago. And it is quite different in the statement than in the testimony which we heard. May I continue, Your Honour, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. What is the question that you wish to put?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour. [Interpretation] I would like to ask the witness how come that in her statement, paragraph 12, when she described the situation she said nothing about Sredoje Lukic being there. There's an important distinction and there is also a discrepancy between the statement and this witness's live evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, madam.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise. I don't know why the name was not included here. Maybe it was simply left out. It could be an error in the actual recording of the statement. Why is it there in number 9 and not in number 12, I don't know. I don't believe this is down to me. Maybe this is a typing error when the statement was copied or a misinterpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Number 9 talks about the description. Number 12 is the about Behija Zukic's car alone and Nikola Vujicic's and Milan Lukic's arrival. Just let me ask my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. I thought you were waiting for my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No. [In English] Just in English scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just I'm trying to understand. Go back to paragraph 12. What is your point, Mr. Cepic? That in paragraph 9 there is a mention of her seeing Sredoje Lukic, and in paragraph 12 there is no mention. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Because the point is she knew him before, she even describe him, but when she described the scene in front of hospital, Visegrad hospital, she just recognised Milan Lukic and Niko Vujicic in paragraph 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But why -- it's not clear to me why it's mandatory that it should be mentioned in paragraph 12 because it was mentioned in paragraph 9. It's not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe we can forgot paragraph 9. Just to focus on paragraph 12. And just to make a question from that paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But that may be the answer. It's already in 9. Anyhow, let's of move on. Let's move on. What is your next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just to see the signature at the bottom of the page, if the court usher could scroll down the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, is that your signature at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, you gave this statement over a period of two days, did you not, to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, one day. It was more or less on one day, and then the next day they read it back to me and I signed it. It took time to translate it and so on, so they came the second day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And did you confirm that the statement is a true rendition of what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks like the square, but at the time the plateau was completely empty, there was nothing on it. Now there is. You had the shops or whatever, the buildings, but at the time there was absolutely nothing there. It was an open space except for the willow tree, that was much smaller at the time. There was nothing else, just the willow and the small house, none of the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you whether this is the location of the square in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be, but I'm not sure. That's all I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, what is the bridge called, the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the Pase Sokolovica bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you recognise whether there are any people on the bridge there or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see anything. I can't make anything out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What does it say there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says Mehmed-Pase Sokolovica Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, can you see anybody on that bridge? Well, if not, how then could you say in paragraph 22 of your statement that from an even greater distance you were able to see somebody coming on to the bridge at night and killing people? How come we have that testimony in paragraph 22 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the car came on to the bridge and parked itself there and that shots were heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, I'm going to quote your statement. [In English] Can we have 22nd paragraph of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just be heard before we move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Sir, could I suggest this is a very dubious technique, presenting a video of nighttime scenes of the area. The witness has indicated she's having some difficulty as indeed I'm sure others are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, he can put it, it's for us to disregard it. I can't prevent him from put ting it. She will say whether it helps her in recognizing the area or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: It's just it's a dangerous technique, with respect, Your Honour. Grainy footage like that of an evening we don't -- I certainly asked previously if we could have some indication of the date, and we have that. We don't have any indication of the time of the night or other matters like that. It's just seems to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It just looks as if you are making a submission that we shouldn't attach much weight to it and maybe we will not. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have 22nd paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were very explicit in your statement, and you said that you saw the accused come to the bridge five or six times, bringing people there and killing them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And you could see that quite certainly. You could see that, but you couldn't recognise the people, that's the only thing. You couldn't recognise the people. But it could be seen, the bridge was lit up --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may be at a disadvantage because of the language situation here, but it seems to me that the witness's answers may be being truncated by my learned friend when she wishes to say something more and he indicates thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There may be a degree of overlapping. Please observe the pause and of course it will not be proper if parts of the witness's answer were eliminated from the record. Now, what was the last thing you said, Witness? You said you "could see that quite certainly, you could see that but you couldn't recognise the people, that's the only thing. You couldn't recognise the people but it could be seen. The bridge was lit up." Did you have anything more to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, the bridge was lit up and the square was too. And you could see him park on the bridge, you could hear shots, you could hear the bodies falling into -- the thump of bodies into the water, that was something that one could hear. You couldn't recognise someone and you couldn't say who had been killed, but you could see it all. And I wasn't the only one to see it. Lots of people were looking at it and saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. And allow the witness to complete her answer in future.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, you'll agree with me that you couldn't see whether Sredoje Lukic was there or not because it was dark and you just said that you couldn't actually recognise the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sentence in which I mentioned Sredoje Lukic in this particular paragraph, I wasn't thinking of that particular incident on the bridge, that Sredoje Lukic was killing. I never saw Sredoje Lukic kill anyone. Never. Nor did anybody tell me that Sredoje Lukic had killed someone. Nobody I ever talked to. However, in this paragraph what I wanted to say is this, and let me repeat it now, that I would see Sredoje Lukic in the company of Milan Lukic, but never, and I state that here and now, I never saw Sredoje Lukic, one, kill anyone, or two, abuse anyone. I never saw that myself and I never said that. I never claimed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And did anybody ever tell you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did anybody ever tell you that they saw Sredoje kill anyone or abuse anyone? Did you ever hear that from anybody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not to me, no. And I can explain a few things. The rumours, when you say somebody said so and so said and then so and so said something else two days later or you heard something else two days later, so I don't want to repeat these rumours from people that would change their accounts from one day to the next. But as I say, no serious-minded person ever told me or nor did I hear them say that Sredoje Lukic killed anybody or abused anybody and towards me his conduct was decent. We came across him in -- I came across him in the MUP. He said hello nicely, warned me not to move around town and left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will agree with me, won't you, that you probably saw Sredoje with Milan somewhere about town and not on the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's precisely what I had in mind. I didn't mean the old bridge and the killings there. You see the way the paragraphs break down and how I gave my statement, but I did refer to this several times. I didn't even see Sredoje with Milan very often either. I can't tell you how many times but it wasn't that often.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry, what was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Admission of video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Video clip bearing number 2D040180 will be Exhibit 2D25, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, you will agree with me that Sredoje Lukic is a positive personality, and a pleasant character and he did not fit into this overall war atmosphere that prevailed at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I agree. I could even tell you my husband

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: then, as well as later, I can only say that I'm surprised and I'm not even sure that I can bring myself to believe some things that are being said about Sredoje Lukic in this negative light.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, madam. Madam, thank you very much. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We need to move to public session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. VG-133, you told counsel in your cross-examination that your husband left Visegrad, I think you indicated sometime in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And what was the village that he went to some distance away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nezuci. The distance being about a kilometre and a half, up to 2 kilometres but no more than that. From the town itself. Perhaps even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And was that village on the side of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't quite on the riverbank. It was further up in the hills on the left-hand riverbank.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How far away was that village from the Varda factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as the crow flies maybe 400 or 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And how long was your husband at this village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband was there -- well, I had left Visegrad on the 17th of June, and he stayed on until the fighting erupted. So it may have been a total of two or two and a half months.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: You told the Court also that your sister's husband went missing and that he hasn't been located. What was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Esad Hajdarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: When did he go missing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He stayed in Visegrad when we left on the 17th of June. He was hiding in the basement of the house in which my sister lived at the time. Nothing has ever been heard of him since.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, page 36 I'm looking at here, you told the Court that -- and we're talking about the events that you witnessed on the 10th of June, 1992, and you've described in detail what you saw from your mother-in-law's apartment balcony that day. You said you mixed up two events when you were describing the events in your statement. You recall saying that in court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I wonder if the statement could be brought up on the screen, paragraph 17. Can you see paragraph 17 in the Bosnian language before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So just so clarify what you said in explanation to counsel, the incident that you describe as being in mid-morning, was it the incident with the Montenegrins that occurred in mid-morning on the day previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So the incident with the Montenegrins occurred the mid-morning on the 9th of June, is that what you are saying, the mix-up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The killing on the bridge could have occurred between half past 6.00 and 7.00 that afternoon. Milan Lukic arrived just before 6.00 p.m., he entered the building, and how long could this possibly have taken. This may have occurred at about 7.00 p.m. that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Right. That was to be my next question. Thank you. You've given us the time, but the date that that occurred was what day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And when you witnessed the killing, what time of day was it in terms of daylight or dark? Could you describe the time of day in terms of lightness or darkness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't dark yet. There was a lot of natural light because it was summertime.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you were asked about the fire at Pionirska Street in June of 1992 by counsel; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you told the Court that there was much discussion about that in Visegrad the morning after it occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not much discussion, rather, people talked to one another, would see one another and tell one another about what had occurred. We were warning each other, saying that the best idea was to probably leave town as quickly as possible on account of that event. On the 14th of June, my mother asked me to leave with my children. My sister and I. However, we were all keeping our fingers crossed, hoping that the whole thing would come to a halt. Nevertheless, once this had happened we too decided to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, you've told the Court, page 48, that you first heard about the fire on the 15th of June, this is 1992, in the morning; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you recall about what time it was you first heard about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite early that morning. That same day, right after 9.00, I went to the Red Cross office to register there with my children in order to leave town. Therefore, we must have been told about that very, very early on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And when did the fire at the Pionirska Street occur or when did you hear it had occurred in relation to the first time you first heard about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard about that that morning. I don't know at what time that occurred. However, this was a word of mouth thing, that's how the news spread. If you knew that there was some other Muslims around, you would go see them to tell them about what was going on and to warn them to move out of the way, as it were, but no one really asked a question as specific as that, when exactly did that occur. The important thing was to inform one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I am sorry. I may not have made myself clear. When did the Pionirska fire occur? What date?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let us see whether she knows. Do you know when the Pionirska fire took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 14th of June in the evening. That's what we heard and we were told the morning of the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I want to ask you about a man that you referred to in your testimony earlier in answer to counsel's question, and my pronunciation may not be the best. A man referred to in your statement at paragraph 25, if that could be shown to you, maybe that's the easiest way. Islam Cormehic. Can you see the name Islam Cormehic or something similar in paragraph 25 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, how well did you know that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you know or do you know his date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. He is older than me, perhaps a year or two older, but I can't be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Is the surname Cormehic unusual or is it a common name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not entirely unusual but it's not very common either. There were perhaps a handful of families there and they were all in Njavjestica [phoen], the neighbourhood that was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Is the first name of Islam a common or uncommon name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps not all too common, but you do come across it every now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And where did this family come from? Where was their home village, the surname Cormehic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know. But I know that all of them lived in Povjestaca. This was the name of the neighbourhood. But I really can't say where they hail from originally.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you have a look, please, at paragraph 12 in your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer will you be because we are at the time for the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm not sure, sir, maybe 10 minutes, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll seek the indulgence of the interpreters and just carry on for 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Paragraph 12, there were some questions about why you didn't -- or why the name Sredoje Lukic doesn't appear in paragraph 12 as being in the Passat at the health centre that day when you have mentioned that in testimony here that he was in the car. Can you just explain why it doesn't appear in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We already heard an answer on that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's hear it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If you could just give us your explanation, please, as to why his name doesn't feature in paragraph 12 about that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I go through paragraph 12 again and once I reach its end, as far as I can tell, in paragraph 12 I describe the behaviour of Milan Lukic and Niko Vujicic. Maybe I didn't have anything special to add about Sredoje's actions or behaviour and that may have been the reason for my omission. One thing I do know is, when I go through the whole thing now, I describe Milan Lukic rolling the window down and grinning at us, and then I go on to explain how the body of Behija Zukic was removed and how her death was established by Dr. Vasiljevic. It's possible that Sredoje Lukic's name was simply omitted from this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Just a couple of more questions for you. You were shown a video of Visegrad a short time ago and (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: That was your apartment, the apartment you witnessed those killings was your mother-in-law's apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The fourth floor and the building number is 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: You were shown in the video a willow tree that you commented on. 16 years ago in 1992, can you recall the size of the willow tree on that occasion? How tall it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't very tall. If I look at the footage, it's very difficult to say, but you can say that it's a great deal larger than it used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: In 1992, did the willow tree obstruct any of your view of the bridge from your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking from this side, I had four windows on that side. And we couldn't see the river from there because of the weeping willow and the house that blocked our view. We could only see the river from the side, the lateral window of my flat. The Visegrad bridge, the hotel, the square, although you could actually see the square from the other windows too but the view was quite poor. The view of the bridge was relatively poor at the time, even when the willow tree was smaller, from those windows, and one couldn't really see the river from those windows. It was only from the side of the building, the windows that were on the side of the building that we could see the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Just finally, the view that you -- the window that you had the best view from in your apartment, was that shown -- the view from that window shown in the video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was all dark. Frankly, I couldn't tell a thing myself. There were some small houses that were built on that square. There is a lot of new construction going on, and I hadn't set eyes on that for 16 years so it all struck me as very new.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Right. That last answer, you are referring to what you could see in the video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. That concludes your testimony. We thank you for giving it and you may now leave. Mr. Groome, are there any other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Just the two witnesses I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, in that event, we will adjourn until tomorrow at 2.15.
